plan.summary: This first 4-week block sets the base for a 12-week off-camp boxing strength and power cycle. Week 1 establishes training maxes for the primary lift so percentage work is grounded in a real baseline, then Weeks 2-4 build lower-body power, full-body strength, trunk stiffness, and a small amount of boxing-friendly conditioning without creating unnecessary fatigue. With only one S&C session each week, the plan keeps the highest-value work first and trims volume so it supports skill practice instead of competing with it. Review progress at the end of Week 4 before the next block is built.

phaseOverview.label: Building
phaseOverview.focus: Build baseline lower-body strength and general power while keeping speed qualities present in a low-fatigue way.

phaseOverview.label: Intensifying
phaseOverview.focus: Progress strength and power with slightly heavier loading while keeping the work crisp and recoverable for boxing practice.

phaseOverview.label: Expressing
phaseOverview.focus: Shift toward faster, sharper force expression with enough strength work to hold onto the gains built earlier.

exercises.name: Box Jump
exercises.notes: Use a box height you can land on quietly and cleanly. Step down each rep and keep every jump fast and crisp.

substitutionOptions.name: Countermovement Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if box setup is awkward. Reset between reps and chase height with clean landings.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if you want an even simpler beginner option. Start from a still quarter squat and jump straight up.

exercises.name: Trap-Bar Deadlift
exercises.notes: Warm up gradually, then work up to one hard set of 3-5 reps with solid form. This establishes your baseline for future percentage work, so stop before technique breaks.

strengthAssessment.prompt: Warm up progressively, then work up to your heaviest clean set of 3-5 reps. Log the load and reps so the app can estimate your 1RM for future percentage-based work.

substitutionOptions.name: High-Handle Trap-Bar Deadlift
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if the low handles are uncomfortable or mobility is limited.

exercises.name: Chest-Supported Row
exercises.notes: Pull hard, pause briefly at the top, and keep your chest glued to the pad. Leave 1-2 clean reps in reserve.

substitutionOptions.name: Seated Cable Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a neutral or close grip and keep the torso steady.

substitutionOptions.name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Brace well on the bench and avoid twisting to finish the rep.

exercises.name: Push-Up
